canonical_topic: Crude oil as a market benchmark
definition: Crude oil is the world's most traded commodity, which gives it outsized influence as a price benchmark across the broader energy sector even where a direct fundamental link is weak.
core_idea: Because crude oil trading volume dwarfs other energy commodities, its price movements are treated as a market-wide signal and often move other energy prices even absent a direct supply/demand connection.
key_points: Crude oil is the single most traded commodity in the world.
This trading dominance makes crude oil prices highly influential across energy markets generally.
Crude oil prices can materially move other energy commodities even when there is no real underlying connection between them.
relationships: Crude oil price acts as a sentiment/benchmark driver for other energy commodities
trading_implications: Traders in other energy commodities should watch crude oil price moves as a market-wide sentiment signal, independent of direct fundamentals.
caveats: A large price impact from crude oil does not imply a real fundamental (supply/demand) link to the affected commodity.
